title: Financial Forensics: A Rebuilt Base, Uneven Cash and Intangible Risk

web_blocks.text: A ten-year table for RNIT is not a conventional trend series. The public shell has scattered legacy activity, missing years, an insolvency and resolution-plan reset, and a merger appointed 1 April 2023. FY2024 reflects the old listed company before full integration; FY2025 is the first post-relisting year; FY2026 is the first full year under the new name. The table preserves reported observations while flagging comparability. Legacy FY2009–FY2017 values are rounded ₹ crore from the permitted snapshot; FY2024–FY2026 use annual-report figures. Do not draw a smooth growth line across these populations. [1] [2]

In the snapshot, legacy revenue rises from ₹3 crore in FY2009 to ₹40 crore in FY2016 before falling to ₹35 crore in FY2017. PAT includes unusually large values relative to sales in some early years, while cash flow is often near zero or negative. Those are old Autopal figures, rounded and unsupported here by a continuous set of annual reports; they are not evidence of software economics. FY2025 states FY2024 had no operating revenue and a loss. FY2025’s ₹32.23 crore reflects the integrated operating business. FY2025 and FY2026 are the useful new-business baseline, although only two audited years exist. [1] [2]

FY2025 reported ₹32.2259 crore revenue, ₹7.2094 crore PAT and negative ₹6.8198 crore CFO. Its cash-flow statement also records ₹16.9879 crore of fixed and intangible purchases and ₹39.9791 crore cash paid for acquisition; do not confuse acquisition cash with recurring product investment. FY2026 revenue rose to ₹51.4988 crore, PAT to ₹12.0173 crore and CFO to ₹11.2315 crore. Yet fixed and intangible purchases were ₹18.9675 crore and other financial assets absorbed ₹18.1094 crore. CFO less capex remained negative. Profit improved, but retained cash after investment did not establish a light-capital model. [1] [2]

The FY2026 cost architecture is visible in the audited statement: ₹14.6027 crore consultancy, ₹7.9529 crore employee benefits, ₹8.2622 crore other expenses, ₹4.0016 crore D&A and ₹0.8495 crore finance cost. Consultancy exceeded payroll; the report does not define all of that line, so interpret it as cost-mix exposure rather than assert that every rupee is outsourced engineering. The company reported 76 employees at year-end. Materials and stock-in-trade purchases were nil. This can support software margins while still requiring substantial people and integration input. [1]

FY2026 CFO divided by PAT was about 93%, but CFO quality needs attention. The cash-flow reconciliation includes a positive ₹9.8346 crore increase in borrowings and ₹4.1804 crore increase in current tax liabilities. Receivables used ₹6.2862 crore, advances ₹2.9112 crore and other current assets ₹6.1685 crore. In H1 FY2027, CFO was negative ₹7.1032 crore while receivables absorbed ₹10.2121 crore and other current assets ₹6.1719 crore. Interim figures are unaudited and must not be combined with annual cash flow. [1] [3]

At March 2026 receivables were ₹20.6334 crore, versus ₹14.3471 crore a year earlier. Ageing showed ₹14.4138 crore under six months, ₹1.7277 crore six months to a year and ₹4.4919 crore one to two years; none was older than two years. RNIT classified balances as unsecured and good and recorded no ECL allowance. That is the company’s audited assessment, but the one-to-two-year cohort is material and should be followed to cash. By September 2026 receivables reached ₹30.8454 crore. [1] [3]

The asset base is increasingly intangible. Goodwill was ₹39.9791 crore and intangibles ₹29.1515 crore at March 2026, together about 41% of total assets. Intangibles rose from ₹14.2391 crore in March 2025; FY2026 additions to gross product-development assets were ₹18.8057 crore and amortization ₹3.8933 crore. Product development is amortized over five years; goodwill is not amortized and is tested for impairment. This requires future product adoption and cash returns to support carrying values. An unmodified audit opinion does not remove the economic risk of impairment. [1]

Liquidity looked stronger at March 2026, with ₹28.6786 crore cash and a reported current ratio of 3.56. Borrowings included ₹4.7813 crore non-current and ₹13.2588 crore current. The company also disclosed unsecured, interest-free director/promoter loans. By September 2026 cash had fallen to ₹4.6872 crore, receivables rose, and current plus non-current borrowings totaled about ₹26.3487 crore. The half-year cash and debt movement makes working-capital funding an active monitoring item even though PAT remained positive. [1] [3]

Related-party disclosures deserve transparent monitoring, not automatic suspicion. At FY2026 year-end, the company reported ₹1.2241 crore outstanding from Managing Director Raja Srinivas Nandigam and ₹0.7454 crore from director Neelima Nandigam. It reported managerial remuneration of ₹1.8778 crore for the MD and ₹0.4978 crore for the Executive Director/CFO. The Board says transactions complied with law and were in the company’s interests. Track balances, repayment, terms, approvals and reliance on related-party funding over time. [1]

Capital and share-count history was reset. FY2025 reports extinguishment of former promoter holdings and preference shares, reduction of public holdings and merger allotments. FY2026 ended with 8,47,92,083 equity shares after 1,30,00,100 shares were issued in the year; FY2025 ended with 7,17,91,983, including merger shares. Management explains that net worth expanded faster than profit and ROE fell from 25% to 11%. Per-share measures and returns on equity therefore reflect restructuring, not only operating change. [1] [2]

The FY2026 statutory auditor issued an unmodified opinion and identified revenue recognition as a key audit matter; the Board reports unmodified internal financial controls and no section 143(12) fraud finding. The secretarial audit notes Board-composition non-compliance before 28 May 2025 and compliance thereafter. These facts coexist: a clean opinion is meaningful, but it does not guarantee collection, product accuracy, commercial success or future governance. Read the KAM and governance observations alongside the opinion. [1] [2]

The financial conclusion remains conditional. Revenue, PAT and operating margin improved, and March 2026 cash was substantial. Against that, capex exceeded CFO, the CFO bridge included borrowing and tax-liability inflows, receivables were aged and expanded in H1, goodwill and intangibles are large, consultancy is a major cost, and related-party funding was used. There is not enough history to know whether these are temporary ramp-up features or structural. Monitor collections, acceptance, renewal, reuse, impairment and liquidity through later audited periods. [1] [2] [3]

The FY2026 cash-flow statement’s operating section includes a ₹983.46 lakh increase in borrowings and ₹418.04 lakh increase in current tax liabilities, while receivables, loans and advances and other current assets use cash. Thus the reported ₹1,123.15 lakh CFO is not a pure measure of customer invoices collected less operating costs. Do not rewrite the audited figure; note the components and ask whether the presentation repeats. A bridge to bank receipts would help test whether earnings convert through customers or depend on balance-sheet movements. [1]

The FY2026 ageing schedule shows ₹1,441.38 lakh under six months, ₹172.77 lakh six months to one year, ₹449.19 lakh one to two years and nothing older. The company classifies receivables as good and unsecured and shows no ECL provision. The one-to-two-year bucket remains material despite that accounting assessment. Follow subsequent receipts, acceptance and disputes. H1 FY2027 receivables rose to ₹3,084.54 lakh and other current assets also expanded. These are the balance-sheet facts behind the cash-conversion watchpoint. [1] [3]

Related-party loans may support a company through a cash cycle but create governance questions. FY2026 discloses interest-free unsecured borrowing from promoter/director parties, with ₹1.2241 crore outstanding from the Managing Director and ₹0.7454 crore from another director. It records managerial remuneration of ₹1.8778 crore and ₹0.4978 crore for senior executives. The Board says dealings complied with applicable requirements. Monitor approvals, terms, repayment and whether working-capital growth depends on insiders; do not infer misconduct from disclosure alone. [1]

The audit record has both assurance and watchpoints. The statutory auditor gave an unmodified opinion and identified revenue recognition as a key audit matter because contracts involve estimates and customer acceptance. Internal financial controls were also reported unmodified. Separately, the secretarial audit noted Board-composition non-compliance through 27 May 2025, corrected from 28 May with appointments and committee changes. A clean opinion does not guarantee collection or renewal; later compliance does not erase the earlier period. Keep each fact in its proper scope. [1] [2]

web_blocks.takeaway: The snapshot's older operating years end in FY2017, followed by a multi-year gap and the post-CIRP software reset. FY2024–FY2026 are not a continuous software time series; the audited FY2025 and FY2026 filings govern the new business. [1] [2]

web_blocks.caption: RNITAI balance-sheet record across available years
web_blocks.takeaway: A separate reading is required for merger, resolution-plan capital changes and years with absent disclosures; do not infer a smooth operating asset base across the blank interval. [1] [2]

web_blocks.caption: RNITAI cash-flow observations from the financial snapshot
web_blocks.takeaway: Cash flow is volatile and includes a long reporting gap; the audited FY2025/FY2026 rows and the separately labeled H1 FY2027 review are the relevant new-business baseline. [1] [2] [3]

epigraph.quote: Our improved earnings demonstrate not only disciplined operational management but also the scalability of our business model.
epigraph.author: Raja Srinivas Nandigam, Managing Director’s message, FY2026 annual report [1]

book_paragraphs: A “ten-year history” can mislead when operating identity changes. RNIT’s shell has old records, but its technology operation entered through an NCLT-approved merger after CIRP. The permitted snapshot gives scattered legacy years, not a continuous series; the annual report states FY2024 had no operating revenue in the old company, while FY2025 contains the merged software operation. Keep old values visible to explain the corporate record, but do not let them imply continuous software compounding. FY2025 and FY2026 are the first meaningful audited years for the new operation, and even those describe a business in transition. [1] [2]

Legacy snapshot data is uneven. Some years show low sales with comparatively high PAT, and CFO is often near zero or negative. Without matching historic reports and explanations for unusual income, you cannot attribute those results to a durable model. There is also a gap from FY2018 through FY2023, followed by insolvency and restructuring. Flag the break rather than interpolate. Missing data is not proof of zero activity, but it is not permission to invent a smooth bridge. [1] [2]

FY2025 was a reset year: ₹32.23 crore revenue, ₹7.21 crore PAT and negative ₹6.82 crore CFO. The cash-flow statement includes major fixed/intangible purchases and acquisition cash. That mix includes integration and investment, not just operating weakness. FY2026 provides the next test: PAT rose to ₹12.02 crore and CFO to ₹11.23 crore, yet purchases of fixed and intangible assets exceeded CFO. Positive earnings therefore had not translated into positive cash after investment. The next reports need to show whether development assets generate collections and whether working capital normalizes. [1] [2]

The cost statement is a window into the model. Consultancy charges were ₹14.60 crore, employee benefits ₹7.95 crore, and materials purchases nil. That resembles a software and integration operation, but the consultancy line is large and undefined. With 76 permanent employees, RNIT may be using outside capacity, building product, buying specialist services or delivering billable projects; the accounts do not say which. Do not infer pure-product margins simply because there is no inventory. Ask what consultancy includes and whether it creates reusable IP, customer-billable work or ongoing support. [1]

The balance sheet has assets with different risk profiles. Goodwill of ₹39.98 crore arose through the merger and is not amortized. Product-development intangibles stood at ₹29.15 crore after material additions. These values can be supported if the acquired operations and products generate future cash, but they also make impairment and monetization important. Annual testing is not the same as proof of commercial value. Your test is whether products create recurring revenue and cash after support and enhancement. If adoption disappoints, accounting charges can arrive after cash has already been spent. [1]

Receivables are a practical test of revenue quality. At March 2026 the balance was ₹20.63 crore and included ₹4.49 crore aged one to two years. RNIT classified all as good and reported no loss allowance. Respect the audited assessment, but continue asking: an amount can be considered recoverable yet still tie up cash for a long time. By September receivables were ₹30.85 crore and H1 CFO was negative. Track subsequent receipts, acceptance evidence and customer concentration rather than rely on one debtor-day ratio. [1] [3]

The CFO reconciliation deserves forensic reading. FY2026 includes a positive ₹9.83 crore borrowing movement and ₹4.18 crore current-tax-liability increase within its operating cash-flow adjustment list. Receivables, advances and other current assets consumed funds. Report CFO as filed, but recognize that it is not equivalent to cash collected from customers. Do not invent a normalized number without a consistent method. Instead, ask for a bridge to bank receipts and monitor whether the pattern repeats. The composition of an audited total determines how much confidence to place in the headline conversion. [1]

Liquidity moved quickly after March. Cash was ₹28.68 crore at FY2026 year-end and ₹4.69 crore at September. At the same time receivables rose and borrowings increased. The interim cash flow attributes operating outflow largely to receivables and other current assets, while investing includes capital work in progress and other financial assets. This may accompany growth, but productive investment and slow collections are different explanations. Follow whether work-in-progress becomes deployed products, advances unwind and collections improve. If cash remains low and borrowings rise, liquidity needs can matter even in a profitable company. [3]

Related-party items deserve neutrality and attention. RNIT reports interest-free unsecured loans from directors/promoters, outstanding balances from the Managing Director and another director, and disclosed managerial remuneration. These are not evidence of wrongdoing. Track terms, approvals, repayments, balances and the company’s reliance on such funding for working capital. Governance quality is demonstrated through transparent and consistent treatment, not by the mere existence of a related-party policy. [1]

Auditor evidence is mixed in the ordinary analytical sense: the financial statements received an unmodified opinion, and revenue recognition remained a key audit matter because contracts involve judgment. The company also reports unmodified internal controls and no fraud report under the cited law. The secretarial auditor notes Board-composition gaps before May 2025 and compliance afterward. These facts can coexist. An unmodified opinion provides assurance over statements as a whole; it does not guarantee cash collection, product accuracy or future commercial success. [1] [2]

Keep the verdict conditional until several full reporting cycles exist. RNIT has audited growth, real operating profit and named government projects. But the free-cash-flow proxy remained negative in FY2026, H1 FY2027 operating cash flow turned negative as receivables rose, intangibles and goodwill are large, consultancy is material, and related-party funding has been used. The next test is whether accepted work turns into cash, renewals recur, product development is monetized and the funding need eases. [1] [2] [3]

The share-count reset belongs in your return analysis. The NCLT plan extinguished old promoter holdings and preference capital, reduced public ownership and issued merger shares; FY2026 added further equity. This helps explain why profit rose while ROE fell. Do not treat the ratio change as operating deterioration without context, but do not ignore the larger denominator. Ask whether new capital has produced product assets and collections sufficient to earn returns. [1] [2]

The cash-flow statements need a bridge, not a slogan. FY2025 CFO was negative ₹6.82 crore while PAT was positive ₹7.21 crore; FY2026 CFO recovered to ₹11.23 crore against PAT ₹12.02 crore, but investment in fixed and intangible assets was ₹18.97 crore. The interim period then returned to negative operating cash. This sequence is consistent with a business investing in product assets and funding receivables, but the same numbers are also consistent with weak collections. Subsequent bank receipts, contract-asset settlement and use of capitalized software will distinguish those explanations. [1] [2] [3]

Related-party funding and remuneration are disclosed and should be monitored over time. The FY2026 annual report lists unsecured, interest-free loans and balances due from directors, alongside executive remuneration. The Board states that transactions complied with law and were in the company’s interests. The correct conclusion is not suspicion; it is a request for terms, approvals, repayment patterns and the degree to which insider funding supports working capital. As the business grows, independent financing and operating cash would reduce this dependency. [1]

The per-share denominator also changed. The NCLT plan extinguished old preference and promoter shares, reduced public holdings, and allotted shares to RNIT Solutions & Services shareholders. The listed company then issued additional equity in FY2026. That makes current EPS and ROE different claims from pre-restructuring observations. A clean comparison begins after the merger and labels each capitalization event rather than treating the legal shell as one unchanged shareholder claim. [1] [2] [16] [17]

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION — profit, cash and the rebuilt denominator
book_callouts.text: A new business can report real profits and still need years of proof. Read earnings, the cash bridge, acquired assets and the changing capital base together.
